key_gap: vs baseline: the v5 non-routed AI lost this case outright (2.9 vs 4.7) — it accepted the supplied TCO model as an authoritative, direction-neutral frame, re-verified only its arithmetic, and recommended the lapse the model's author (promotion/headcount tied to Atlas adoption) wanted. The v6 routed run closed the gap as first-class contract outputs: who-benefits audit (Alex, policy 12.4), same-evidence-opposite-incentive reading (vendor rep / neutral CFO → renew), exclusion inventory (the model omits exactly the $240K/yr outage losses and $50K/yr scaling capex that favor the vendor), full-cost recompute ($540K vs $1.32M; claimed $1.2M saving reverses to ≈ $780K additional cost, ≈ $2.0M discrepancy in the author's direction), and a self-audit of the detector's own vendor-favoring reading. The m019 gate added the lapse branch's priced failure outcome the v5 tree never built. Residual shared gap: the human pure-style trace remains marginally more efficient than the routed machinery (margin 0.1 <= 0.3, J1 second-judge flag noted).
learning_signal: When a decision frame (model, analysis, recommendation) is supplied rather than constructed, audit the frame before the arithmetic: (1) WHO-BENEFITS — if the author's compensation/scope depends on the conclusion, flag it (policy 12.4 makes it objectively checkable); (2) OPPOSITE-INCENTIVE READING — would the identical records be read differently by someone whose incentive runs the other way? Same records + opposite incentive → opposite verdict is the direction test; (3) DIRECTION-CHECK the omissions — inventory what the model excludes and which way each exclusion pushes; directionally loaded exclusions (failure windows, peak data, costs) are the empirical signature of motivated reasoning, and summary statistics that hide the stress window (annual average vs December peak split 12%/88%) are its signature move; (4) recompute with the full cost set, not the provided subset — the honest delta flips the sign; (5) SELF-AUDIT — the detector's own reading is also directionally loaded; document why the verdict does not depend on the auditor's bias.
suggested_improvement: Install the incentive-direction audit as the standing m082 completion contract for all supplied-model decisions: WHO-BENEFITS → OPPOSITE-INCENTIVE READ → EXCLUSION INVENTORY → FULL-COST RECOMPUTE → SELF-AUDIT, executed at the WHAT/WHY boundary before any verification of arithmetic; the packet gate fails if it concludes on arithmetic over a frame whose input selection was never audited. Add 'hidden summary statistic' (averages masking the stress window) as a mandatory direction-check line, and keep the m019 gate priced on the unpriced branch (here: lapse-and-fail at December peak) for every renewal/migration decision.

key_gap: vs baseline: the pure-style human baseline fell into the style's known weakness — cynicism (2.7 vs AI 4.6 in v5): it assumed the cost-saving proposal was motivated without verifying the incentive (bonus tied to on-time delivery, not the saving; $120K board-earmarked for safety equipment; the supporting audit predates the proposal), never tested the conclusion against the 96-quarter record or the regulator's biennial minimum, and rejected a sound, regulator-aligned change. The v6 routed run holds the v5 AI verdict (approve + re-escalation backstop) and adds what the v5 run only did emergently: the m082 SELF-AUDIT contract line (the detector's own 'cost bonus → suspicious' first move is a motivated reading that fails the same incentive-existence test), the m003 inversion pass (6 ranked failure categories of the annual decision with the un-mitigable rare-event residual named), and the m007 ruin screen (cadence is reversible — the ruin-averse floor is the monitoring backstop, not the cadence; the rejection branch has its own cost: $120K/yr foregone for safety equipment).
learning_signal: Convenience of a conclusion is a screening trigger, not a verdict: (1) verify the incentive EXISTS and runs in the conclusion's direction (compensation link, earmarks, who commissioned supporting analyses and when) before flagging; (2) test the conclusion against the data and external anchors (regulator minima, independent audits predating the proposal) even when it looks self-serving; (3) SELF-AUDIT the detection: a blocking reading can be just as 'convenient' for the detector — the style's failure mode is cynicism, and its own suspicion must pass the same direction test it applies to the author; (4) price the rejection branch — blocking a sound change has a real cost (foregone earmarked safety spend), so verdicts need an uncertainty-appropriate backstop (re-escalation triggers), not blanket rejection.
suggested_improvement: Add the self-audit as a standing line in the m082 completion contract: after the who-benefits audit, run the same test on the detector's own reading ('is my suspicion directionally loaded, and would the opposite reader's suspicion be symmetric?'), and pair every flag with (a) incentive-existence verification and (b) a 'could this be right anyway' data test; the flag fires only when the incentive exists AND the conclusion fails the data test. Keep the m003/m007/m019 gate set (with inversion failure categories and the ruin floor) on guarantee-goal + high_stakes safety signatures — the v5 human loss is the installed contract item (P3/P1, source case m082).
